text.p: Creditanstalt-Banverein, Austria's number two bank, said on Thursday credit risk provisions had fallen to 3.1 billion schillings in 1996 from 3.4 billion a year ago, defying a rise in Austrian insolvencies.
"The reduction of risk costs, achieved despite persistently large insolvencies, is due to consistent risk management," the bank said in a statement.

Earlier, the bank said 1996 net profit had risen to 2.6 billion schillings from 2.166 billion in 1995, while operating profit -- which according to Austrian law is calculated before risk provisions -- was up at 6.2 billion schillings from 6.138 billion a year earlier.
The number of Austrian insolvencies rose to a new post-war high of about 5,400 last year, some eight percent higher than the previous year's figure.
